body.statement:
Let \(\mathcal W\) be a finite observed vector containing a treatment subvector \(\mathcal X\) and a single finite outcome vertex \(\mathcal Y\).  Let \(\mathbf Q_0\) and \(\mathbf Q_1\) be finite SCMs with positive rational local tables such that \(P_0(\mathcal W=w)=P_1(\mathcal W=w)\) for every observed cell \(w\), but, for some assignments \(x,y\),
\[
 P_0(\mathcal Y=y\mid\operatorname{do}(\mathcal X=x))
 \ne
 P_1(\mathcal Y=y\mid\operatorname{do}(\mathcal X=x)).
\]
Append binary vertices \(\mathcal C\) and \(\mathcal S\), driven by private exogenous variables independent of the old exogenous variables, and use the same new kernels in both SCMs.  For rational numbers \(g_u(c)\) satisfying \(g_u(c)>0\) and \(\sum_{c=0}^1g_u(c)=1\) for every outcome value \(u\), choose rational \(\lambda_c\) such that
\[
 0<\lambda_c<\min_u g_u(c),
 \qquad c\in\{0,1\},
 \qquad
 \Lambda:=\lambda_0+\lambda_1,
\]
and set
\[
 P(\mathcal C=c\mid\mathcal Y=u)=g_u(c),
 \qquad
 P(\mathcal S=1\mid\mathcal Y=u,\mathcal C=c)
   =\frac{\lambda_c}{g_u(c)}.
\]
Then the two extended SCMs are positive and rational and, for \(j\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
 P_j(\mathcal W=w,\mathcal C=c,\mathcal S=1)
   &=P_j(\mathcal W=w)\lambda_c,\\
 P_j(\mathcal S=1\mid\operatorname{do}(\mathcal X=x))
   &=\Lambda,\\
 P_j(\mathcal C=c\mid\operatorname{do}(\mathcal X=x),\mathcal S=1)
   &=\frac{\lambda_c}{\Lambda},\\
 P_j(\mathcal Y=y,\mathcal C=c\mid
       \operatorname{do}(\mathcal X=x),\mathcal S=1)
   &=P_j(\mathcal Y=y\mid\operatorname{do}(\mathcal X=x))
     \frac{\lambda_c}{\Lambda}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Consequently the full selected observational laws and every positive conditioning denominator agree, whereas the displayed selected joint numerators and conditional causal effects disagree.  Graph membership has the following conditional form only: if the two base SCMs have a common represented graph \(\mathcal H\), if \(g_u(\cdot)\) is nonconstant in \(u\), and if \(\lambda_c/g_u(c)\) is nonconstant in \(c\) for at least one fixed \(u\), then every proposed parent is active and both extensions have the common represented graph obtained from \(\mathcal H\) by adjoining \(\mathcal Y\to\mathcal C\), \(\mathcal Y\to\mathcal S\), and \(\mathcal C\to\mathcal S\).
body.proof_tex:
Because \(0<\lambda_c<g_u(c)\), both
\(\lambda_c/g_u(c)\) and its complement lie strictly between zero and one.  All new table entries are rational, so appending the two private-noise mechanisms preserves positivity and rationality.  Also,
\[
 0<\Lambda=\sum_{c=0}^1\lambda_c
 <\sum_{c=0}^1g_u(c)=1.                                      \tag{1}
\]
Appending children does not change the old marginal law.  If the outcome component of \(w\) is \(u\), the SCM factorization and the two displayed new kernels give, for each \(j\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
 P_j(\mathcal W=w,\mathcal C=c,\mathcal S=1)
 &=P_j(\mathcal W=w)
   P(\mathcal C=c\mid\mathcal Y=u)
   P(\mathcal S=1\mid\mathcal Y=u,\mathcal C=c)\\
 &=P_j(\mathcal W=w)g_u(c)\frac{\lambda_c}{g_u(c)}\\
 &=P_j(\mathcal W=w)\lambda_c.                              \tag{2}
\end{aligned}
\]
The division in (2) is legitimate because \(g_u(c)>0\).  Summing (2) over \(w\) and \(c\) yields \(P_j(\mathcal S=1)=\Lambda\); hence equality of the two old observational laws implies equality of the two normalized full selected observational laws,
\[
 P_j(\mathcal W=w,\mathcal C=c\mid\mathcal S=1)
 =P_j(\mathcal W=w)\frac{\lambda_c}{\Lambda}.              \tag{3}
\]

Under \(\operatorname{do}(\mathcal X=x)\), modularity leaves both appended child mechanisms unchanged.  Summing out the old variables other than \(\mathcal Y\) in the analogue of (2) gives
\[
 P_j(\mathcal Y=u,\mathcal C=c,\mathcal S=1
      \mid\operatorname{do}(\mathcal X=x))
 =P_j(\mathcal Y=u\mid\operatorname{do}(\mathcal X=x))
  \lambda_c.                                               \tag{4}
\]
Summing (4) over \(u,c\), over \(u\), and then dividing by the positive quantity \(\Lambda\) from (1), respectively, proves
\[
\begin{aligned}
 P_j(\mathcal S=1\mid\operatorname{do}(\mathcal X=x))
   &=\Lambda,\\
 P_j(\mathcal C=c\mid\operatorname{do}(\mathcal X=x),\mathcal S=1)
   &=\frac{\lambda_c}{\Lambda},\\
 P_j(\mathcal Y=y,\mathcal C=c\mid
       \operatorname{do}(\mathcal X=x),\mathcal S=1)
   &=P_j(\mathcal Y=y\mid\operatorname{do}(\mathcal X=x))
     \frac{\lambda_c}{\Lambda}.                           \tag{5}
\end{aligned}
\]
The denominator in the second line of (5) is common and positive.  The strictly positive multiplier \(\lambda_c/\Lambda\) in the third line shows that the assumed interventional disagreement gives unequal joint numerators.  Dividing the third line by the second shows that the selected conditional effect is exactly the old effect,
\[
 P_j(\mathcal Y=y\mid\operatorname{do}(\mathcal X=x),
       \mathcal C=c,\mathcal S=1)
 =P_j(\mathcal Y=y\mid\operatorname{do}(\mathcal X=x)),   \tag{6}
\]
so the effects disagree as well.

For the final graph assertion, independent private exogenous variables and the displayed kernels add no parent other than the displayed old outcome and new conditioning vertex.  Nonconstancy of \(g_u(\cdot)\) in \(u\) makes \(\mathcal Y\) active for \(\mathcal C\).  Since every \(\lambda_c>0\), the same nonconstancy makes \(\lambda_c/g_u(c)\) nonconstant in \(u\) for some fixed \(c\), so \(\mathcal Y\) is active for \(\mathcal S\); the last stated hypothesis makes \(\mathcal C\) active for \(\mathcal S\).  Thus, under the explicitly stated common-base-graph and active-parent hypotheses, both extensions have exactly the claimed common represented extension.  No graph-membership conclusion was used without those hypotheses.
body.justification: The lift converts an ordinary positive rational causal witness into a denominator-locked selected conditional witness by a constructive common child and selection mechanism.
body.gap: An ordinary hedge pair need not preserve a selected conditioning denominator, so an explicit equalizing construction is required.
body.consumer: The informative table proposition instantiates this lift, and future graphical synthesis may use it whenever a common represented base witness is available.
